content:
maria: Heads-up — tokenizers 0.13.3 -> 0.13.4 has an RCE-ish CVE (CVE-2026-0001 in our tracking). Repro: CI started failing on wheel resolution and our KMS integration tests started throwing `InvalidSignature` after the bump.

anil: Seen the advisory. link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-0001. Severity marked HIGH by the scanner.

kevin: Repro log from a failing CI run: 
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for tokenizers which use PEP 517 and cannot be installed directly
File ".../cryptography/hazmat/..." InvalidSignature: signature mismatch
```
CI uses manylinux2014 images.

jenna: Short summary of impacts: 1) host builds for `pip install tokenizers` fail on some runners, 2) our KMS client tests that sign payloads break (looks like `cryptography` got upgraded transitively), 3) audit events for KMS key use appear missing in a few integration runs.

maria: Proposed immediate triage steps: 
- Lockfile regen attempt on a branch to pin safe tokenizers/transformers.
- Run full integration with KMS + RBAC e2e.
- Add an audit logging assertion to prevent silent regressions.
- If CI still broken, consider short-term runtime guard to skip new tokenizers wheels.

kevin: Quick attempt: `poetry lock --no-update` didn't help (lock already had older tokenizers), `poetry update tokenizers transformers` yields dependency conflicts with starlette pinned in our constraints.

maria: Commands I ran locally: 
```bash
# try a targeted update
poetry add tokenizers@^0.13.4 --lock
poetry lock
# or regenerate entirely (takes >30m in CI)
poetry lock --no-interaction --verbose
```
Got starlette conflict: transformers -> starlette>=0.20 but we had 0.18.x pinned in constraints for older FastAPI compat.

anil: On RBAC/KMS side: the audit logs missing thing smells like boto3/botocore version skew: new cryptography + botocore binary wheels produce different sig behavior in our test harness. Also check our KMS client wrapper — we added a subtle retry in mid-2025 that swallows certain 403s.

sec-bot: Automated note: CVE-2026-0001 flagged for tokenizers; recommended actions: backport patch to supported branches, regenerate lockfiles, and produce disclosure timeline.

ops-bot: CI error snippet from runner-42: 
```
Collecting tokenizers==0.13.4
  Using cached tokenizers-0.13.4-cp39-cp39-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl
ERROR: cryptography 41.0.0 has external build dependencies not present: rustc required
```
So some runners don't have Rust toolchain -> wheel fallbacks failing.

jenna: That explains wheel build failures. For mitigation: ensure manylinux wheel install (prefer-binary) or pin cryptography to a wheel-friendly version in constraints to avoid source builds. Also add a CI matrix runner with rust toolchain to catch this earlier.

kevin: Short-term patch I can try: add `--prefer-binary` to our pip step in CI and add `pip install -U pip setuptools wheel`. Could avoid rust builds for cryptography. Also add `TOX_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1` env when running tests that don't need native extension.

maria: Longer-term: we should do these in the change set: 
- Regenerate poetry.lock with updated tokenizers + transformers, bump starlette to 0.20.x where compatible.
- Add integration test asserting KMS audit event presence after key use.
- Add CI pin / prefer-binary to avoid build-from-source surprises.
- Backport patch and release on our LTS channel.

anil: I can take RBAC/audit follow-ups: confirm whether our CloudTrail/KMS logging settings are unchanged and whether the client wrapper retry swallows audit events. I'll run the KMS smoke across branches.

kevin: I'll open a hotfix PR that: bumps `cryptography` to a wheel-available version in `ci/constraints.txt`, adds `--prefer-binary` to the pip step, and adds a short integration test that runs only in canary.

jenna: I'll update test plan for adding an explicit assertion that `kms:GenerateDataKey` usage shows up in the audit stream and fail build if missing. Also add a short note to runbook about adding rust toolchain on runners as an FYI.

maria: Thanks — assigning tasks: @kevin handle CI hotfix PR, @anil investigate RBAC/audit wrapper, @jenna update tests, I'll do the lockfile/regeneration and open backport PRs. If anyone hits blockers ping me in this thread. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Opening PR now and will link here: 2134568001 (placeholder PR link will be posted).

anil: Found one quick cause for audit events missing: our test harness was swallowing `x-amz-request-id` due to a header-normalization change in botocore 1.29.6 -> 1.29.7. Will draft a tiny fix to preserve headers.

maria: Cool. We're tracking on security board and I'll create incident ticket with CVE reference and PR checklist. I'll update when PRs are green.

sec-bot: Reminder: please add CVE and fix PRs to the security board and tag with "cve-fix" label for compliance reporting.

maria: Follow-ups: I'll also add a short postmortem note once we ship. Thanks all. :handshake:
